title: Canary warmup prefetch triggers eviction storm and allocator baton corruption (hosted/dedicated/private)
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Summary: During a canary rollout for an async model warmup/prefetch feature we observed correlated GPU OOMs, a spike in eviction activity, and progressive fragmentation of allocator slabs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Multiple customers reported degraded latency and failed requests.

Impact: Several Dedicated pools reached sustained OOM conditions causing request retries and failovers; Hosted experienced transient capacity loss on a small set of regions; a single large Private customer saw degraded throughput on on-prem nodes and opened an escalation.

Root cause: The new prefetch/warmup path asynchronously populated the serving node's KV cache and occasionally touched ephemeral allocation paths. Under certain multi-tenant load shapes this caused a condensed eviction wave: the eviction subsystem aggressively tombstoned entries while the allocator's baton handoff (a lockless fast-path used during session handover) hit a rare concurrency interleaving that produced double-free-like slab corruption and high external fragmentation. The tombstone buildup further inflated index state and delayed GC, creating a feedback loop culminating in repeated GPU OOMs.

Fix implemented: 1) Emergency toggle to disable async prefetch at runtime and force sequential warmup while we investigated. 2) Hotfix in allocator baton to serialize the critical handoff in the pathological path and add defensive checks to avoid double-free of slab segments (PR runtime#1234). 3) Evictor tuning: added a capped backoff and a token-bucket to smooth eviction bursts. 4) KV index hygiene: introduced a tombstone compaction sweep that runs when index density exceeds threshold. 5) Added a GPU OOM alert runbook step to auto-disable prefetch on repeated OOMs for a host.

Rollout and verification: Patch merged and staged through canary, regional, and global rollout. We monitored the GPU OOM rate, eviction rate, allocator fragmentation metric, and tail latency. Post-rollout metrics: GPU OOMs reduced by ~96% in impacted pools, eviction spikes flattened, and tail latency returned to baseline.

Follow-ups and long-term work: 1) Add an integration test that simulates prefetch under multi-tenant eviction pressure. 2) Replace the temporary serialization with a lock-free baton redesign (ENG-680112). 3) Improve tombstone reclamation thresholds and add a per-tenant index health signal to the Console. 4) Update the canary rollout checklist to include warmup stress scenarios.

Related artifacts: Confluence incident timeline and postmortem, runtime PR, dashboards, customer communications (links below).
